subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the young woman from <Picture 1>, with the same short navy-blue bob haircut, teal-blue eyes, black beret with gold trim and decorative ornaments, navy-and-white academy-style outfit, oversized white sailor collar, mustard-yellow diamond-pattern tie, gray pleated skirt, navy knee-high socks, black Mary Jane heels, small waist accessories, natural body proportions, and realistic appearance.
<Subject 2> is the warm red-walled bedroom from <Picture 2>, including the red walls with dark lower paneling, parquet wooden floor, yellow bed and bedding on the left, crowned plush figure near the bed, wall shelf and books, central vintage television and cabinet, coat stand, black door on the right, red sofa edge, ceiling, wall lamps, decorative objects, warm lighting, and spatial layout.
<Video 1> provides only the complete dance choreography, pose sequence, body rhythm, hand gestures, leg movement, facial-expression timing, full-body framing, fixed-camera behavior, and 8.38-second temporal structure.
<Audio 1> is the synchronized audio track embedded in <Video 1>.

summary:
[reference generation, audio reuse] Generate <Subject 1> performing the complete dance choreography from <Video 1> inside <Subject 2>. Preserve the character identity and costume from <Picture 1>, the bedroom identity and objects from <Picture 2>, and the dance timing and synchronized music from <Video 1>. Do not retain the original dancer or the original hallway.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain her facial identity, navy-blue bob haircut, teal-blue eyes, beret, sailor-collar academy outfit, yellow tie, pleated skirt, socks, shoes, waist accessories, clothing colors, and body proportions throughout the full-body dance.
<Subject 2> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - retain the room’s red walls, dark paneling, parquet floor, yellow bed, crowned plush figure, shelves, books, vintage television, cabinet, coat stand, black door, red sofa edge, lighting, materials, and warm visual identity, while recomposing the wide reference environment naturally into a vertical 9:16 frame without stretching.
<Video 1> (dance, movement, expression, framing, and timing): weak_reference - use only its exact choreography, rhythmic timing, pose transitions, facial rhythm, full-body scale, and fixed-camera presentation; do not retain its dancer, clothing, hallway, doors, walls, floor, or lighting.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - preserve the original music, beat, rhythmic accents, ambience, and sound effects without changing their timing.

detailed_description:
A realistic full-body dance performance inside the warm, stylized-realistic bedroom from <Picture 2>. Integrate <Subject 1> naturally into the room with matching warm light direction, floor contact, shadows, perspective, and environmental reflections. The wide room reference must be vertically recomposed rather than horizontally compressed: place the open parquet floor in the center, retain part of the yellow bed and crowned plush figure on the left, retain the vintage television and cabinet in the rear, and retain the black door and a small portion of the red sofa on the right. Keep sufficient clear floor space around the dancer. Do not generate subtitles, captions, logos, watermarks, interface graphics, or additional text.

[Shot 1] Preserve the single continuous fixed-camera shot and exact 8.38-second timing of <Video 1>. Use a vertical 9:16 full-body composition. <Subject 1> stands in the open floor area at the center of <Subject 2>, facing the camera, with her entire body and shoes visible throughout. She reproduces the dance from <Video 1> frame by frame: beginning in the same relaxed central stance, transitioning into the same lively arm movements and rhythmic weight shifts, lifting one lower leg backward while balancing naturally on the supporting foot, opening both arms with matching wrist and hand shapes, then lowering the leg and continuing the alternating arm pattern. During the middle section, she follows the same hip and shoulder rhythm, brings one hand near her chin while the other arm crosses her torso, and repeats the compact pose at the original beat. During the final section, she releases the crossed-arm pose, resumes the outward hand gestures, shifts her weight, and reaches the same concluding pose and facial expression as the source dancer.

Match every beat, pause, foot placement, balance change, knee bend, hip shift, shoulder rhythm, elbow angle, wrist rotation, finger gesture, head tilt, gaze direction, blink, smile change, and pose transition from <Video 1>. Preserve <Subject 1>'s short hair, face, beret, yellow tie, sailor collar, skirt, socks, shoes, waist accessories, anatomy, and identity through all motion. Her skirt, tie, short hair, and accessories respond naturally to movement without changing design. Maintain realistic shoe contact with the wooden floor and moving shadows consistent with the room lighting. Prevent long-hair reappearance, source-costume contamination, identity drift, duplicated limbs, incorrect leg bending, sliding feet, floating shoes, fused fingers, unstable hands, background warping, object duplication, or facial deformation. Completely exclude the original dancer and original hallway environment from <Video 1>.

overall_soundscape:
Fully preserve <Audio 1>, including the original music, beat, rhythmic accents, room tone, and movement sounds. Synchronize <Subject 1>'s steps, leg lift, hand gestures, pose changes, and ending motion with the original beat. Add only subtle natural shoe contact and clothing movement that fit the bedroom acoustics.

non_diegetic_music:
Use the original music contained in <Audio 1> without replacement, additional music, remixing, or timing changes.
